To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) learning an agent that interacts in a sparse way with the environment can be beneficial for exploration and 2) the use of a latent slot-structured transition can be a powerful tool to bias perception and exploration towards entity-centric grouping.

1) we introduce a model that jointly models perception and transitions, 2) we show that learning a model that assumes sparse transitions biases the model to learn a more entity-centric perceptually grouping, and 3) we show that the model can use this entity-centric grouping as a source of intrinsic motivation.
(i)  the perception module of SPECTRA learns to decompose the visual scene into entities, and (ii) the transition module of SPECTTRA learns to predict sparse transitions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two questions. (1) Can we learn to decompose the visual scene into entities? (2) Can we learn an agent that maximizes the number of entities changed in its trajectory?
the question: How can we exploit the sparsity of the transitions between visual scenes to improve the performance of RL agents?
two questions: How can we model sparse transitions from raw visual observation and what can be learned from such model?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work proposes a novel approach to learning entity-centric representations of the environment and a new exploration strategy for sparse reward tasks.
we present a new model for learning sparse transitions in RL from raw visual observations.
SPECTRA is a model for learning entity-centric transitions that enables the agent to learn to interact with objects in the visual world.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SPECTRA is a novel model that can learn to perceive objects in the environment, and learn to take actions that change them in a sparse way.
our approach enables the agent to learn to act in a more entity-centric fashion, i.e. to learn a model of the world where the objects in the visual scenes play a central role.

we propose a model for learning sparse entity-centric transitions that is able to discover objects in the scene, and learn a policy that maximizes the number of objects affected in the agent’s actions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by jointly learning a perception module with a sparse transition model, we can bias the agent’s perceptual grouping towards objects and encourage the agent to explore more effectively.
learning a perception model jointly with a sparse transition module can lead to better perception and exploration.
by leveraging the sparsity of the transition model, it is possible to learn a perception model that is both entity-centric and sparse.
